Chapter 7: Living as the Beloved—Identity Beyond Shame
You know, there’s this deep desire inside all of us to feel truly loved—not for what we accomplish, but simply for who we are. But shame? It’s sneaky. It keeps telling us we’re not enough, that our shortcomings are all anyone will ever see. Have you ever worried that if people really knew your struggles, they might turn away?
Picture a teenager who’s always felt like she doesn’t quite belong. She hides behind grades, behind being the “good kid,” but inside, she’s terrified someone will see her doubts. One night, she opens up to someone she trusts, expecting disappointment. But instead, she hears words she’s never dared to believe: You are loved, just as you are.
Can you imagine how that would feel? Those words sink in, slowly rewriting the old story of shame she’s carried for so long.
The truth is, a lot of us don’t realize just how much our lives are shaped by this fear of being rejected. We push ourselves to prove we’re worthy, hoping to silence those doubts, but all it does is leave us tired and feeling even more alone. What if I told you that your identity doesn’t depend on how well you perform or how perfect you are? That it’s actually rooted in something much deeper—your belovedness.
Living as the beloved means letting go of those old scripts—the ones that say you’re only as valuable as your last achievement, or as flawed as your worst mistake. It’s about trusting, deep down, that you are cherished. The real journey isn’t about working to become lovable; it’s about waking up to the love that’s already been there all along.
And when you start to live from this place, things really do change. Shame loses its grip. You don’t feel the need to hide as much. Relationships get deeper, and suddenly, you find the freedom to be honest—both with yourself and with others.
Here’s the thing: the gospel isn’t just good news for someday, far off in the future. It’s an invitation to live right now, fully seen, fully known, and deeply loved.
